title: Adaptive Disentangled Transformer for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation seeks to mine time-aware user interests by modeling sequential behaviors.

gap.claim: Existing Transformer architectures lack explicit regularization for layer-wise disentanglement, limiting the use of disentangled representations and leading to suboptimal recommendation performance.

contributions.claim: The Adaptive Disentangled Transformer framework adaptively determines the optimal degree of attention-head disentanglement within different layers.

The framework encourages disentanglement through mutual-information-based independence constraints over attention heads and auxiliary objectives intended to prevent information collapse into useless noise.
A progressive scheduler adaptively adjusts disentanglement-control weights through an evolutionary process.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed ADT framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation models time-aware user interests from sequential behaviors, and Transformers have shown strength in capturing sequential relations.
Existing Transformer architectures lack explicit layer-wise disentanglement regularization, resulting in suboptimal performance.
The paper introduces ADT to adaptively determine layer-specific attention-head disentanglement.
ADT uses mutual-information-based independence constraints, auxiliary objectives, and a progressive scheduler to control disentanglement.
The authors report effectiveness on various real-world datasets.
